([[Greenwood, Indiana]]) | college = [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] (2019–2023) | highlights = * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2023]]) * Third-team All-American – [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]], ''[[Sporting News|SN]]'' ([[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021]]) * [[Karl Malone Award]] (2023) * First-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2022–23 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2023]]) * First-team All-Big Ten – Media ([[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2021]]) * Second-team All-Big Ten (2022) * Second-team All-Big Ten – Coaches (2021) * Third-team All-Big Ten (2020) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2020) * 2× Big Ten All-Defensive Team (2022, 2023) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019]]) * [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] (2019) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|FIBA U18 Americas Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|2018 St. Catharines]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Trayce Jackson-Davis''' (born February 22, 2000) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. ==High school career== Jackson-Davis attended [[Center Grove High School]] in [[Greenwood, Indiana]]. As a junior in 2017–18, he averaged 21.9 points, 9.4 rebounds, 4.1 blocks, and 2.6 assists per game while shooting 67.0 percent from the field; he helped his team to a 20-win season, county and sectional titles and the 4A regional final. In AAU basketball, on the Spiece Indy Heat, he averaged 19.1 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game while shooting 59.1% from the field.{{cite web |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/j/jackson-davis-trayce.aspx|title=Trayce Jackson-Davis|date=January 15, 2019|access-date=March 30, 2019|work=USA Basketball}} During his senior season, he led the Trojans to a 21–8 record and a berth in the Class 4A state tournament semifinals. He averaged 21.6 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.9 blocks, 1.7 assists and one steal per game through 29 games. He entered the state semifinals with 1,768 career points.{{cite web |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/trayce-jackson-davis/37138|title=2018 – 2019 INDIANA BOYS BASKETBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR: Tracye Jackson-Davis|work=Gatorade Player of the Year|date=March 15, 2019|access-date=March 30, 2019}} On January 24, 2019, Jackson-Davis was announced as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] to participate in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019 game]],{{cite web |url=https://www.thedailyhoosier.com/indiana-signee-trayce-jackson-davis-is-named-a-mcdonalds-all-american/|title=Indiana Signee Trayce Jackson-Davis is Named a McDonald's All-American|date=January 24, 2019|access-date=March 30, 2019|last=Schumann|first=Mike|work=The Daily Hoosier}} where he finished with 7 points, 5 rebounds, and 1 block in 14 minutes. ===Recruiting=== He was rated as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[247Sports]], and [[ESPN]]. During his high school career Jackson-Davis was recruited by numerous high-profile schools, including [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], ==College career== [[File:Trayce Jackson-Davis.jpg|thumb|left|Jackson-Davis (right) in January 2020]] Jackson-Davis made his college debut for Indiana during the [[2019–20 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2019–20 season]] with eight points and six rebounds in a 98–65 win over [[Western Illinois Leathernecks men's basketball|Western Illinois]].{{cite news |title=Hoosiers rout Leathernecks 98–65 in opening night hit |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166018 |accessdate=November 6, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} Jackson-Davis was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] co-freshman of the week on November 18, after contributing 20 points, eight rebounds and three blocked shots against [[North Alabama Lions men's basketball|North Alabama]].{{Cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2019/11/18/indiana-michigan-state-and-ohio-state-earn-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=Indiana, Michigan State and Ohio State Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors|website=Bigten.org|accessdate=November 19, 2019|date=November 18, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} He was again named conference freshman of the week on December 2 after scoring 21 points and grabbing 11 rebounds in a victory over [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs men's basketball|Louisiana Tech]].{{Cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2019/12/2/indiana-maryland-michigan-claim-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=Indiana, Maryland, Michigan Claim Weekly Men's Basketball Honors|website=Bigten.org|accessdate=December 3, 2019|date=December 2, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} On February 19, 2020, Jackson-Davis set career-highs with 27 points and 16 rebounds in a 68–56 win over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].{{cite news |title=Jackson-Davis career game leads Indiana past Minnesota 68–56 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166234 |accessdate=February 25, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 19, 2020}} At the close of the regular season, Jackson-Davis was named to the Third Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media as well as the All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |accessdate=March 9, 2020}} He averaged 13.5 points, 8.4 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Beas |first1=Mike |title=Jackson-Davis eager for sophomore season |url=https://dailyjournal.net/2020/09/09/jacksondavis_eager_for_sophomore_season/ |access-date=December 8, 2021 |work=[[Daily Journal (Franklin, Indiana)|Daily Journal]] |date=September 9, 2020}} He finished second in the league in field goal percentage (56.6%), and seventh in blocked shots (1.9) and rebounds (8.4). Jackson-Davis, who started in each game his freshman season, was one of only four freshman in the country to lead his team in scoring, rebounding, free throw percentage and blocks. As a sophomore during the [[2020–21 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2020–21 season]], Jackson-Davis averaged 19.1 points and 9.0 rebounds per game. Jackson-Davis garnered several awards at the close of the season. He was named a third team All-American by the Sporting News, NABC and USBWA; an honorable mention All-American (AP); All-Big Ten (First Team by media and AP; Second Team by coaches); and a Wooden Award Finalist.{{cite news |last1=Rabjohns |first1=Jeff |title=Indiana's Trayce Jackson-Davis named AP Preseason All-American |url=https://247sports.com/college/indiana/Article/Indianas-Trayce-Jackson-Davis-named-AP-Preseason-All-American-173853447/ |access-date=December 8, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=October 25, 2021}} In the offseason prior to Jackson-Davis's junior year, the [[2021–22 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2021–22 season]], [[Mike Woodson]] was hired as head coach of the Hoosiers and Jackson-Davis Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} As a junior, he averaged 18.3 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. He became the second player in Indiana history (with [[Alan Henderson]] with 1,500 points, 750 rebounds, and 150 blocks, and ranked 15th on Indiana's all-time scoring list with 1,588 points, ninth in rebounds (797), seventh in blocked shots (178), and seventh in field-goal percentage (55.8%). On April 9, 2022, Jackson-Davis declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Schumann |first1=Mike |title=Trayce Jackson-Davis declares for 2022 NBA Draft |url=https://www.thedailyhoosier.com/trayce-jackson-davis-declares-for-2022-nba-draft/ |website=The Daily Hoosier |access-date=April 19, 2022 |date=April 9, 2022}} On May 20, 2022, Jackson-Davis announced his withdrawal from the draft and his return to Indiana.{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=May 20, 2022 |title=Trayce Jackson-Davis returning to Indiana Hoosiers after withdrawing from NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33952075/trayce-jackson-davis-returning-indiana-hoosiers-withdrawing-nba-draft |access-date=July 30, 2022 |website=ESPN}} Heading in Jackson-Davis's senior year, the [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2022–23 season]], he garnered substantial national recognition. However, he was raised by his mother and step-father, Raymond Jackson. Originally, Trayce just went by the last name of Davis; however, entering his freshman year of high school, he decided to hyphenate his last name and add on Jackson. He stated, “When I got to high school, I didn’t think it was fair. Ray raised me my whole life, so I did Jackson-Davis. They both want the best out of me, but I would say they do it at different angles."{{cite web |url=http://www.dailyjournal.net/2018/01/09/trayce_jacksondavis_feature___jan_8/|title=Center Grove standout is making the best of both worlds|work=Daily Journal|date=January 8, 2018|accessdate=March 30, 2019}} Trayce has two sisters, Caida Davis and Arielle Jackson, as well as a younger brother Tayven Jackson. Tayven was a high school teammate at Center Grove. Tayven went on to play quarterback in college for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|University of Tennessee]] for one year before transferring to [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana University]], where he has four years of eligibility. On March 15, 2019, Jackson-Davis was honored as the [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Indiana Gatorade Player of the Year]].
